transport: FishNet LAN, standalone host and independent clients on one machine
checks: Two real RPC requests competed for one rank. One reply accepted, one rejected; the treasury was charged once.
The remote client aimed the cabinet, observed the requested cage in flight before credit, and got one free item on contact.
The server rejected a dispenser request from the research terminal and rejected a full selected stack without firing.
A missed charge reached the floor. E transferred it once, and retrying the old serial produced no second item.
The receiver equipped and returned the charge using slot 2. Research increased the capacity of slot 1 and taking another cage cost nothing.
Each process rendered the active sample mesh for both issued cage shots and the missed charge.
The assisting player inherited the same physical cage after its carrier disconnected, released it, and the host reloaded the saved fleet.
All peers matched the full fleet manifest, old-depth traps, reservoir, treasury and ranks. Only the owning client received its private slot data.
The same profile rejoined twice. Disconnecting during the last charge flight canceled the parcel, left the profile revision unchanged and credited no item.
testSetup: The host seeded trial materials and loaded fleet stock, teleported divers into reproducible poses and moved the intended recipient away to force a miss. Purchases, dispensing, pickup, equipping and returning equipment used real owner RPCs.
diagnostics: Each batch player logged two AudioClip.SetData failures in TechRigShell.Tone. Each host also logged a missing U+2713 glyph in PTSans-SDF. No managed exception or save error appeared in these six player logs.
